Pain thresholds and tolerance were also assessed.

memory: The effect of green tea (GT) on post-exercise fat oxidation compared to placebo was examined in studies involving both trained and untrained males. One study found that fat oxidation was significantly increased post-exercise in the GT group compared to placebo (p < 0.01). Participants ingested GT or placebo capsules 24 hours before exercise sessions. A double-blind crossover design was used, with a washout period of at least two weeks. Blood lactate levels and RQ were measured. The study included 28 healthy, non-smoking males, with trained participants being cyclists and triathletes. Another study noted that GT may enhance fat oxidation by inhibiting norepinephrine breakdown. These findings suggest that GT supplementation may increase post-exercise fat oxidation. The studies were approved by relevant ethics committees, and participants provided informed consent.

memory: The study [PMC1261533] compared artemether-lumefantrine (ALN) with mefloquine-artesunate (MAS3) in treating malaria. It was an open-label, randomized trial involving 452 patients from Thailand, including displaced Karen people and migrant workers. During follow-up, 119 (26.3%) had P. vivax parasitaemia. MAS3 had significantly fewer cases (29 of 227) compared to ALN (90 of 225) (P < 0.001). The trial was approved by Mahidol University’s ethical committee. Patients with fever or malaria symptoms had blood smears taken. Adverse events were monitored at each visit. Resistance to either drug could affect both combinations.

memory: The study [PMC2974815] compared a "phone calls" group with a "no phone calls" group on treatment discontinuation. Patients were randomized to receive either active telephone calls or no calls, alongside two treatment regimens: "traditional" (diuretics and beta-blockers) or "current" (angiotensin II antagonists and calcium channel blockers). Significantly fewer patients in the "phone calls" group discontinued treatment (4 vs. 30; p<0.0094). The research was conducted at the Hypertension Unit, University of São Paulo General Hospital.
text: Patients in the "phone calls" group had significantly lower treatment discontinuation rates (4%) compared to the "no phone calls" group (30%; p<0.0094) [PMC2974815].

memory: Notes for the next step: The study [PMC5588958] investigated the effect of 28 days of oral SRT2104 (2.0 g/day) versus placebo on body weight in people with T2DM. It was a prospective, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study approved by the MHRA and conducted at the Wellcome Trust Clinical Research Facility. Body weight decreased by 0.93 kg (95% CI −1.72 to −0.15, p=0.0236) with a treatment-by-period effect (p=0.080). Safety assessments included blood tests for haematological, biochemical, and liver/renal function parameters. The study adhered to the Declaration of Helsinki. No other sources directly addressed the effect of SRT2104 on body weight in T2DM.

memory: The study examined the effect of the Sonas programme on MMSE scores in individuals with moderate to severe dementia. Participants were recruited from nursing homes and stratified by MMSE score (0–10 and 11–20). A reading group was used as a control to account for attention effects. Significant improvements in communication ability were found in the Sonas group compared to the reading group at baseline and follow-up for those with MMSE scores of 0–10 (p = 0.011, p = 0.044) and 11–20 (p = 0.026). No difference was found between the Sonas and control groups. The study excluded individuals with major depression, severe pain, or prior Sonas exposure. Informed consent was obtained from next-of-kin for those with dementia.

memory: The study compared meditation awareness training (MAT) with a control group on workaholism symptomatology. MAT included guided sitting, walking, and working meditation, aiming to enhance awareness and ethical clarity. MAT participants showed significant, sustained improvements in workaholism symptoms compared to controls. Participants were allocated to MAT or a waiting-list control group based on availability and matched on demographics. Mixed effects models assessed outcomes like BWAS, DASS, and work engagement. No participants had recent drug use, alcohol consumption, or sleep disorders. Ethical considerations included informed consent, acknowledging MAT's secular use of Buddhist techniques. The study's design controlled for variables like sleep, lifestyle, and employment type. Excluded were those who couldn’t attend required sessions. Source: [PMC5520118], [PMC4663570].
text: Meditation Awareness Training (MAT) significantly reduced workaholism symptomatology compared to a control group, with sustained improvements observed. This conclusion is supported by the study [PMC5520118].

memory: Notes for the next step: The study compared face-based attentional bias modification (ABM) with placebo on anxious symptoms. During positive ABM, participants learned to direct attention toward positive stimuli, while placebo ABM had probes equally often appearing behind positive and negative stimuli. Anxiety symptoms, measured using the STAI trait subscale, showed a significant reduction in the positive face ABM group during follow-up (t(15) = 2.4, p = .03). Participants were blinded to group allocation, and the study was approved by an ethics committee. Salivary cortisol and self-reported symptoms were collected, with saliva samples obtained using a salivette device. The study design ensured randomization and adherence to ethical standards.

memory: The study [PMC1868022] evaluated the impact of a Pap smear on cervical inflammatory responses, including IL-10 levels. Cervical vault lavage (CVL) samples were analyzed using a commercial CBA system. Following a Pap smear, IL-10 levels, along with IL-12 p70 and TNF-α, were significantly elevated, while IL-8, IL-1β, and IL-6 remained unchanged. Participants were randomly assigned to intervention (Pap smear) or control (no intervention) groups. The study was approved by the University of Cape Town's Research Ethics Committee, and informed consent was obtained. The other articles [PMC5452353, PMC5264222] are unrelated to IL-10 and Pap smears.

Venous blood samples were collected biweekly for metabolic and hematological analysis, and pregnancy tests were conducted for women of childbearing potential. memory: The study compared Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) with individual support (IS) on felt stigma in women. Results showed that women in the CPT group experienced a significantly greater decline in felt stigma compared to IS participants at the end of treatment (B = −0.44, p = 0.02). CPT may address overgeneralized perceptions by helping survivors identify support sources and disconfirm negative beliefs. The study was conducted in accordance with ethical guidelines and included participants with breast cancer and bone metastases. Participants in both groups experienced a reduction in stigma over time, but CPT showed a more substantial effect. The trial was designed to assess the composite endpoint, and safety evaluations were based on all randomized patients who received at least one dose of study drug.
text: Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) significantly reduces felt stigma more than individual support (IS) in women with breast cancer and bone metastases (B = −0.44, p = 0.02). Both groups showed stigma reduction, but CPT had a greater effect.

memory: The study compared a weight management intervention targeting diet and physical activity plus usual care with usual care, focusing on fiber intake at 12 months. The intervention included monthly booster sessions and skills training for behavior change, with self-monitoring and relapse prevention strategies. It resulted in significant improvements in fiber intake (M between-group difference = 5.7 g/day, p < .001) and weight loss at 12 months (M difference = −1.85 kg, p = 0.1). The study used a randomized controlled trial design with opaque, sealed envelopes for allocation. Participants received feedback based on ESM data, and the intervention aimed to test theoretical models of behavior change. Data were collected alongside qualitative interviews and fidelity checks.
